newsitem.title: FRANCE: S&P keeps Alcatel under credit watch.
newsitem.headline: S&P keeps Alcatel under credit watch.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday that it kept the long-term "AA-" and the short-term "A-1+" debt ratings of Alcatel Alsthom on creditwatch with negative implications.

In a statement, the ratings agency said a left wing victory in French parliamentary elections made "very unlikely" the privatisation of a part or of the whole Thomson group in the near future and this meant that Alcatel debt would not be negatively affected by potentially winning the right to purchase the state's majority stake in Thomson-CSF.

"The outcome of the French parliamentary elections held on June 1st 1997, very much reduces the likelihood that the Thomson group would be partly or totally privatised short-term. Alcatel has applied for the majority of Thomson-CSF's stock. Standard & Poor's considers that this possibility no longer impacts Alcatel's creditworthiness," the statement said.
France's Socialist party, which won power in Sunday's parliamentary elections, have not yet clearly stated their plans in regard to privatisations set by the previous centre-right coalition.

S&P also said that in spite of the strong net debt reduction resulting from a large assets sales programme started in 1996, consolidated margins and cash flows remained in 1996 well below levels reqired for the current ratings.

"The outcome of the current creditwatch will therefore partly rely on Standard & Poor's anticipations on the group's recovery in terms of operating margins and of its ability to generate future free cash flow in a very competitive industry," it added.
